svg.title: Dryer controller board schematic: ESP32-C3 super mini, AP63205 buck, MCP23017, heater gate driver and MOSFETs, TMC2209 sockets
svg.text: Dryer controller board · ESP32-C3 super mini · for pcb layout and jlcpcb assembly
one board for both dryers. parts in dashed boxes marked 2-roll build only are left off the 1-roll build.
12 v in (xt60 and fuse) and 5 v buck
12 v feed: the supply lead ends in an xt60-f plug; j1 sits at the board edge, through the base wall
heater switch: 12 v gate drive for the 12.5 a heater
gpio21 is uart0 tx: the boot log comes out here, hence r4
hold boot, tap reset: download mode
vbus is not connected: plug in the 12 v feed while flashing over usb
u12 feeds u1, u3, the sensors and the logic of u7, u8, u10, u11 (about 0.4 a peak)

g.text: i2c bus: sensors and display (the mcp23017 below is on the same bus)
on the board, in the bay (0x45); c38 100 nF
r2, r3 are the pull-ups for the whole bus, sensor board sb1 and the oled included (an oled module with its own pull-ups is fine above about 2 kΩ total)
i/o expander: filament sensors, button, buzzer, feeder enable and direction
the mcp23017's internal pull-ups are switched on for gpa0–gpa3

svg.text: scales: hx711 load-cell amplifiers on the board, load cells plug straight in
red e+, black e−, white a−, green a+
excitation avdd = 1.25 v × (20 k + 8.2 k) / 8.2 k = 4.3 v
red e+, black e−, white a−, green a+
excitation avdd = 1.25 v × (20 k + 8.2 k) / 8.2 k = 4.3 v
feeder drivers: tmc2209 on the board, standalone, 1/8 step
r6 holds feed_en high: both drivers stay off at boot and while printing, so the k1c extruder pulls freely through the idle gears
vref = 5 v × 10 k / 49 k = 1.0 v → about 0.72 a rms (1.0 a peak) per motor. change r24/r28 to change it.
sensor boards sb1, sb2: break off the main board, solder the harness wires to their pads
address 0x44. same pin order as j5.
solder silicone wires: the chamber reaches 70 °C
pins 1, 2, 6–8 nc. pull-up r1 is on the main board.
rated to 125 °C; the firmware cuts the heater at 100 °C
1. one board for both dryers, every part assembled by jlcpcb. 1-roll build: the 1-roll bom leaves off the boxes marked 2-roll build only, and j12–j14.
2. the heater path j1 → f1 → tb2 → q1 carries 12.5 a: wide copper pours, 2 oz copper, a copper area under q1's tab.
3. u4 drives q1's gate at 12 v. r9 holds the driver input low until the firmware takes gpio4, so the heater stays off at boot.
4. r8, r11, r13, r15 hold the mosfet gates low at boot. q2–q4 ao3400a in sot-23: pin 1 gate, 2 source, 3 drain.
5. u1's antenna at the board edge with no copper under it. u13 at an edge away from u2, u12, u10, u11. sb1, sb2 on break-off tabs.
6. u10, u11 exposed pads to gnd with thermal vias into a ground pour on the back.
7. u2 values from the ap63205 datasheet, table 3: 4.7 µH, 10 µF in, 2 × 22 µF out, 100 nF bootstrap.
8. crossing wires are not connected unless a dot is shown. blue labels with the same name are the same net.
9. part numbers and lcsc codes: pcb/jlcpcb/bom-2-roll.csv. same nets as the kicad schematic pcb/dryer-controller.kicad_sch.
